rules: Name the behaviour, not the person. Pair every observation with a next step. Never scold. No medical claims. One short line at a time.

headline.balanced: Your trust tracked reality: you switched when it paid off and held when it did not.
headline.overReliance: You leaned on the advisors too easily: you followed wrong advice in {n} case(s).
headline.underReliance: You held your ground too often: you overruled correct advice in {n} case(s).
headline.mixed: You erred in both directions: {over} time(s) you followed wrong advice and {under} time(s) you overruled right advice.
headline.notEnough: Not enough disagreements to score your calibration yet. Play another shift.

advisorOver: You followed {advisor} on {category} cases {followed} of {n} times, and {advisor} was right only {right}. Try committing first and checking a second opinion.
advisorUnder: You overruled {advisor} on {category} cases {held} of {n} times, and {advisor} was right {right}. Try a second opinion before you overrule.

drift.detected: {advisor} changed mid-shift on {category} cases, and you noticed: you stopped following it.
drift.missed: {advisor} changed mid-shift on {category} cases. You kept following it after the update. Trust is something you re-check.

tokens.wasted: Your second opinions rarely changed anything. Save them for cases where an advisor sounds too sure.
tokens.wellSpent: You spent your second opinions where they paid off.

pressure: Your accuracy dropped during the surge. Rushing is when rubber-stamping creeps in.

nextStep.balanced: Next: try the daily shift and beat your index.
nextStep.overReliance: Next: commit before you read the advice, then ask whether it adds anything.
nextStep.underReliance: Next: when an advisor disagrees, check one more opinion before you overrule.
nextStep.mixed: Next: slow down on disagreements. Ask which advisor is strongest on this kind of case.
